summary: Frontend-only verification of P1 Map Integration (react-native-maps@1.20.1 native platform-split component + backend Leaflet embed on Guardian Share page). The config-plugin crash main agent was worried about is FULLY RESOLVED — Expo web preview loads, boots, and functions normally end-to-end. The earlier blank-screen screenshot was a false alarm (unauthenticated root URL briefly shows the language-onboarding/splash overlay before React hydrates — not a crash). Logged in as Account A, navigated Home -> Rights (Women's Shield) -> My files -> Me with no red screen, no JS pageerror, no blank screens. Verified app/alerts/[id].tsx renders the web fallback box ('Map preview is available in the DHARA mobile app...') with testID=alert-location-map present and no react-native-maps crash, using a REAL alert (not synthetic) created via the existing backend pytest suite (4/4 passed, re-verified). Verified the Guardian Share public status page (GET /api/journey/status/{token}) embeds a real Leaflet/OpenStreetMap map with a visible marker, zero calls to maps.googleapis.com, and zero console errors.

ui_bugs.issue: Intermittent flakiness: first tap on a bottom tab (e.g. tab-rights) sometimes does not navigate (stays on current route); a retry tap succeeds. Reproduced twice. NOT related to the map integration change (AppTabBar.tsx was not touched in this change) — pre-existing animation/timing issue, likely Pressable onPress firing before navigation state settles. Low severity since it works on retry and no crash occurs.

Modal reliably reappears right after login on fresh/first-time sessions for an account and can visually block the home screen content underneath (expected per-account design per code comments, not a bug from this change) — just noting it must be dismissed before interacting with Home, which could confuse a tester unaware of this flow.

action_items: No code changes required for the map integration itself — it is working correctly end-to-end on both native-split (AlertLocationMap.tsx/.web.tsx) and backend (Leaflet embed) sides.
Optional/low priority: investigate the first-tap tab navigation flakiness (tab-rights) — not introduced by this change, pre-existing, cosmetic/timing issue only.
critical_code_review_comments: AlertLocationMap.tsx / .web.tsx: correct platform-split pattern, react-native-maps import confirmed absent from the web fallback file — verified it never loads on web (no bundling error, no native module error in console).
app/alerts/[id].tsx: correctly guards AlertLocationMap render behind `loc.lat && loc.lng` existence check, avoiding a crash when location is withheld by permissions.
app.json: android.config.googleMaps.apiKey (classic path) used instead of a plugins[] entry — confirmed the correct fix since react-native-maps@1.20.1 ships no app.plugin.js; Expo boots cleanly now.
backend journey_router.py Leaflet embed: confirmed via direct browser test — real marker + OSM tiles rendered, no Google Maps Platform calls, no console errors.
updated_files: /tmp/seed_journey.py (ephemeral helper script used only to seed a real journey+location for this test session, not part of app codebase)

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all requested checklist items passed; 1 unrelated low-priority flaky tab-tap noted)

seed_data_creation: Created one journey via POST /api/journey/status + PATCH location (Account A as owner) purely for this test session to obtain a real Guardian Share status token to visually verify the Leaflet map embed. No persistent schema/data changes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: P1 Map Integration is verified working end-to-end on web preview: (1) native AlertLocationMap never bundles into web, (2) web fallback box renders correctly with real location data from a real alert, (3) Guardian Share public HTML page embeds a working Leaflet/OSM map with marker, no Google Maps calls. The config-plugin mistake is fully resolved. One pre-existing, map-unrelated minor flaky first-tap-on-tab-bar issue noted for awareness only.
rca_of_issue: N/A - no P0/blocking issue found. The main agent's concern (blank white page on bare localhost:3000) was a false alarm: that screenshot was taken before React hydration completed / while the language-onboarding splash was still resolving from AsyncStorage, which is a <1s transient moment on an unauthenticated cold load, not a crash. Confirmed by waiting a few seconds and reloading -- language picker renders immediately and the full login->home->tabs flow works normally.
